name: Mivrel Sorrel-Coconut Cream
description: A family-run Tier 1-2 brand producing a cream soda that blends synth-sorrel tartness with coconut cream flavoring, sold in recycled 500ml bottles with hand-applied paper labels in the Shelf's Eastern Corridor markets.
flavor_profile: Bright, tart hibiscus-adjacent sorrel tang layered over a sweet, fatty coconut cream base, with a slightly grainy texture from the synth-cream emulsifier.
slogan: Tastes like home. Whatever home means.
cultural_context: Mivrel is one of the few remaining family-operated beverage producers on the Shelf, and locals buy it partly out of genuine affection and partly as an act of economic solidarity. The hand-labeled bottles are a point of pride — and a production bottleneck.
story_hooks: A corponation acquisition team has been making increasingly aggressive offers to Mivrel's elderly founder — and the founder's adult children are divided on whether to sell.
The recycled bottles Mivrel uses are sourced from a collection network that has started disappearing; someone is disrupting it and it's unclear why.
A batch of Mivrel was contaminated with a mild euphoric compound — the family swears it was accidental, but someone on the Shelf thinks it was a test.
